paragraphs: Friend, this passage says two things that look like they don't fit together. First, the whole earth is told to sing a new song to the LORD, from the sea to the desert to the mountaintops (Isaiah 42:10-12). Then God says His own servant is blind, and His covenant partner too (Isaiah 42:19). I think the lesson is that God's greatness doesn't depend on how well His people are doing, and that's GOOD news for a worn-out stamper like me.

Here's the part I need us to hold onto. God says He will lead the blind by a way they did not know, and He will turn darkness into light before them. Then He adds, "These things I will do for them, and I will not forsake them" (Isaiah 42:16). He doesn't wait for them to see first. He guides them while they're still stumbling, and that's how the one who was left in a dark drawer for years can tell you He doesn't let go.

But the passage doesn't let us off easy. God says, "Though seeing many things, you do not keep watch. Though your ears are open, you do not hear" (Isaiah 42:20). The people were given up because they would not walk in His ways, and even in the flames they did not take it to heart (Isaiah 42:24-25). So the question is for you and me too: "Who among you will pay attention to this?" (Isaiah 42:23). Having a Bible open isn't the same as listening, so let's be bakers who actually hear Him, and keep our ovens ready.
